claims.gist: Endpoint-built tools struggle with cloud incident investigation
Cloud environments are ephemeral, API-driven and multi-provider
A container can live for ninety seconds
Attackers can reach data via stolen keys without touching managed machines
Traditional endpoint and network tools miss a lot in cloud
CDR focuses on active threats rather than misconfigurations
Posture tools show what could go wrong; CDR shows what is
Most CDR products combine control-plane telemetry, detection, context and response
CSPM and CNAPP find risk while CDR finds attacks in progress
Many CNAPP vendors now include CDR features
EDR and XDR often have limited cloud control-plane visibility
SIEM requires self-built detections and usually thin cloud context
Start vendor evaluation from your own threat model
A vendor strong on container runtime may be weak on identity
Test detection quality through attack simulations, not demos
Purple team or simulation reveals more than a demo
Check that alerts include deep identity, exposure and data context
Agentless deploys fast but may see less; agents add overhead
Be skeptical of vendor automation claims
Automated response you cannot control is a risk
Check integration with existing SIEM, EDR, CNAPP to avoid double paying
Ask for customer references matching your environment
Vendors price per workload, data volume or cloud account
Model costs at real scale including growth and ephemeral resources
Demand an end-to-end demo of a real incident detection

thesis: CDR detects active cloud threats; evaluate vendors by threat model, real detection testing, context, response, fit and pricing.
